GRAIN. One row per FILE, not per line. A line number is not a stable identity:
an edit above a site renumbers it, which would fire the ratchet on a whitespace
change and let a real regression hide inside the churn. The file is the unit a
fix is actually made in. Every line, arm and source text is named in the row us
why, and the per-file SITE COUNT is carried in arm, so 8 sites collapsing to 1
still reads as a shrink even though the row survives.
ARMS A and B carry NO residual doubt — a caught throw is I-could-not-look by
construction, and an optional-CALLED method may not exist. ARM C carries
declared doubt, and the gate prints that doubt as UNPROVEN on every run rather
than hiding it inside the count.
THE STANDING EXAMPLE. room.boundingWallIds ?? [] recurs across this ledger.
C78 §0.g measures boundingWallIds as HARDCODED [] by both CreateFloorCommand and
CreateCeilingCommand, and §0.3 records that rebuildSemanticGraph us boundedBy arm
reads it at the WRONG PATH. So the field is empty at the writer, misread at the
rebuild, and defaulted to empty at every reader — the same fact denied three
times over, and every ?? [] listed here is the third denial.
EXIT CONDITION (C78 §20, U-INV-4 row): no ?? [], ?. or catch-arm on a discovery
path collapses failure into emptiness — i.e. swallowed reaches EMPTY. A row
leaves this list in the commit that makes its file return a determination; a row
no longer measured is STALE and exits 3. The list may never grow.

this number smaller (roadmap §0.1). Red at a named ledger IS the deliverable.

STRUCK 2026-08-13 (second lane) — ConstraintEngine.ts, the ARM B row, and the
SHARPEST instance measured so far because its output is COMPLIANCE ADVICE a
human acts on. Four tier-1 rules made one hop as
`roomStore.getRoomsAdjacentToWall?.(wallId) ?? []`. Each builds a POSITIVE
membership set and then asserts on its ABSENCE, so a store lacking that one
method did not merely lose a check — it INVERTED three verdicts against a
valid model: ROOM_NEEDS_DOOR emitted severity 'error' "no door found on any
bounding wall" citing Part B fire egress for EVERY room; HABITABLE_NEEDS_WINDOW
the same; and ACCESSIBLE_ROUTE printed "widest door is 0mm" citing BS 8300 —
a measurement of a door it never read. This is the FacadeOrientationService
shape (C79 §5.2.0): an absence becoming a positive, regulation-citing claim.

validateAll as a before/after diff, so phantom errors became phantom
CONSEQUENCES shown pre-commit, and WorldModelAdapter feeds them to an LLM.

STRUCK 2026-08-13 (second lane) — WorldModelAdapter.ts, the A+C row, and the
WIDEST-TRAVELLING instance in this ledger: its output leaves the type system
entirely and becomes English. Six store reads were written
`try { return _store('wallStore')?.getAll?.() ?? []; } catch { return []; }`
— ARM A and ARM B stacked. A store absent from `window` (load-order race,
project isolation) and a store that threw both produced [], which the adapter
counted into wallCount/totalElements and toPromptContext SERIALISED INTO AN
LLM PROMPT. The model was told in JSON that the building has no walls, then
asked which walls could be removed. Two siblings closed with it:
getComplianceContext's outer catch returned passRate: 1 with zero violations
— an INFRASTRUCTURE FAILURE rendered as a fully compliant building; and
`(room.boundingWallIds ?? []).length` reported boundingWallCount: 0, i.e.
"this room is unbounded", about a room nobody measured (C79 §7.1). Closed by
packages/ai-host/src/storeReadDetermination.ts. TWO members are in play and
the distinction is load-bearing: RELATIONSHIP_NOT_READABLE for an absent or
throwing SUBSTRATE, RELATIONSHIP_NOT_RECORDED for a FIELD no producer wrote.
Counts are `number | null` and null is never 0; passRate is null and never 1
OR 0, since both are positive claims; and renderCount emits the WORD
"unknown" so no model can reason from a fabricated zero.
